text:
elaine: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about an impersonation workflow for background jobs (cron/orchestration) that need cross-project access. want to avoid long-lived api keys tied to service owners. ideas? :thinking:
jack: +1 we keep hitting this. current pattern is project-scoped API key per job which is awful for rotation and RBAC.
mayur: TL;DR: prefer ephemeral, brokered tokens minted per-run with tightly-scoped claims (project, role, TTL). no long-lived keys except the broker's credential.
tess: Sounds good. questions: who vends the tokens? the job runner (orchestration service) or a separate token-broker microservice?
elaine: leaning token-broker. single auditing point, easier to enforce policy and rotate broker identity. also allows attestation checks before minting.
jack: agree. tradeoffs: more latency per-run for minting, and we need to batch renewals for high-throughput fan-out jobs. we should consider pre-warmed tokens or TTLs aligned with job lifetime.
mayur: We can support two issuance modes: on-demand (fresh token per run) and lease (short-lived multi-run token with N uses). enforce TTL + usage_count in broker.
tess: RBAC mapping: broker should accept intent & target-project id + requested role. then check the caller's identity and policy. important: deny cross-org escalation.
elaine: policy semantics: allow service_actors to request impersonation only if caller has binding to "impersonate" for the target role. map to existing RBAC proto: request {subject, target_project, role, purpose}. broker checks policy engine (opa) and issues JWT-like token with claims: iss=bkr, sub=service:orchestrator, act=impersonated-service, proj=target, role=..., exp=...
jack: snippet of token shape we discussed:

```
{
  "alg": "HS256",
  "iss": "token-broker",
  "sub": "svc:orchestrator-1",
  "impersonated": "svc:data-processor",
  "proj": "proj-42",
  "role": "storage.write",
  "use_count": 1,
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

note: keep token compact and verifiable by resource services via broker's public key.
mayur: Audit and attribution: resource services should log both token.sub (caller) and impersonated principal. that preserves operator-level attribution while showing which actor actually performed the action. add an "audit_path" claim with broker request id to link broker logs + resource logs.
ops-bot: deploybot: new config for token-broker will be rolled in staging on monday — @tess @jack please check. :gear:
elaine: Security concerns: if broker credential is compromised -> huge blast radius. mitigation: HSM-backed key, mutual-TLS for broker endpoints, and least-privilege for broker signing key (rotate frequently, KMS/HSM audit). Also consider multi-sig for high-privilege impersonations.
tess: Another edge: offline jobs running for hours. we shouldn't issue a single long-lived token. suggest session heartbeats: job holds a short token and periodically re-attests to broker (attestation can be ephemeral pod identity or signed run metadata) to extend. if broker doesn't get heartbeat, token invalidated.
jack: Operationally: need quota controls and rate-limits on broker to avoid RPS avalanche. also graceful fallback policy: if broker unavailable, jobs can optionally fall back to queued-mode (enqueue and retry) instead of using stale long-lived keys. no silent grace.
mayur: Implementation plan: phase 1 - broker MVP that mints single-run tokens for orchestrator. RBAC check via OPA, sign with KMS. phase 2 - add multi-run leases, heartbeat, attestation. phase 3 - integrate with auditing UI and per-token cost attribution in billing.
elaine: Open questions for RFC thread: 1) token format — JWT vs compact signed bundle? 2) whether to support service->service direct impersonation (without broker) for low-latency hot paths. 3) migration path for existing long-lived project API keys.
jack: My take: use compact signed JWT (RS256) to leverage existing libs. disallow direct S->S impersonation except for a handful of low-latency internal paths (must be approved). migration: create broker-minting shim that accepts old API key and issues ephemeral tokens for compatibility.
mayur: I'll draft the follow-up RFC section for "broker security model" and "audit linking". ETA EOD Wednesday.
tess: I'll put a short runbook for broker outage modes + rollback steps.
elaine: Awesome — next steps: mayur RFC, tess runbook, jack prototype PR for token schema. tagging for visibility: @security-team @platform. thanks all. :thumbsup:
